gitCommit.subject: Apply category rules on every statement import path
gitCommit.body:
Apply category rules on every statement import path

Category rules only ran inside TextWithAiHandler's parser-first branch, so
the vision_ai strategy — the default for new accounts — imported straight
from the AI's categorization and never consulted the user's rules. A rule
taught by correcting a transaction had no effect on the next statement.

Move the matcher into ImportFinalizer, the one point every strategy passes
through, and apply it after extraction so a rule overrides the AI rather
than racing it. The pre-AI pass in TextWithAiHandler is removed: with the
finalizer applying rules for all three strategies, keeping it would only
double-count hits.

Make "contains" survive the same transaction being phrased differently
between imports. The AI keeps or drops an embedded account number, so a
rule learned as "pago de prestamo total de recibo" never matched
"PAGO DE PRESTAMO 9837815631 TOTAL DE RECIBO". A contains rule now also
matches when the pattern's words appear in order with gaps between them,
on top of the plain substring that short patterns like "oxxo" rely on.

Deliberately not a similarity score: two loans at the same bank differ only
by their account number and score ~0.85 on trigrams, so any threshold loose
enough to bridge that gap also merges two different debts.

Order rules by pattern length within a priority, so the rule naming a
specific account beats the generic one that would otherwise swallow it —
every learned rule shares priority 0 and ties were resolved arbitrarily.

Add CategoryRules::Backfiller and a rake task to re-apply rules to
transactions imported before the rule existed. It previews by default: a
rule's category cannot be told apart from one the user set by hand
afterwards. Updates go through update! so the auto-link callback moves a
corrected row onto its debt or saving.

Fix the Nueva Regla button, which was invisible on desktop. The hand-written
display-utility block in application.tailwind.css redefines .hidden after
Tailwind's own utilities and re-emits only md:block/flex/grid/hidden, so
"hidden md:inline-flex" could never resolve. This was the only such element
in the app; the override block itself stays because two buttons in
transactions/index rely on it.

Announce the feature in /guides, and fix two pre-existing e2e failures found
while covering this: the inline-category test filtered on a fixed prefix that
matched every earlier run's leftover rows until the new pair fell off page 1,
and the settings toggle test reloaded before its form submission landed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
